title: Open-source telephony core
summary: Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, Kamailio, and rtpengine do different jobs. The pages below say which job each project claims.

lessons.title: Four projects, four roles
lessons.summary: Read the role each project states. Do not treat them as four names for one PBX.
objectives: Place Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, Kamailio, and rtpengine
Say which one is a media proxy meant to sit with Kamailio
Refuse a single configuration that the pages do not share

illustration.title: Integration map, from the project pages
illustration.caption: Kamailio can sit in front of a PBX. rtpengine proxies the RTP. This drawing is that relationship, not a production size.

layers.name: Kamailio
layers.detail: Open source SIP server. Proxy, registrar, load balancer, WebSocket.

layers.name: Asterisk or FreeSWITCH
layers.detail: Dialplan and endpoints. Kamailio's page names both as systems it can front.

layers.name: rtpengine
layers.detail: RTP and other UDP media. Meant to be used with Kamailio. GNU/Linux.

layers.name: SIP dialog
layers.detail: Still RFC 3261. These programs do not replace the protocol.

paragraphs: The Asterisk history page says the project was published under the GPL and that the idea of an open source PBX caught on. Current SIP configuration for the PJSIP channel driver is documented as res_pjsip and chan_pjsip, in pjsip.conf, with extensions.conf as the dialplan.

The FreeSWITCH manual this lab opened teaches SIP profiles, the dialplan, codec selection, media handling, WebRTC, and the Event Socket. It says FreeSWITCH ships as Open Source FreeSWITCH and as FreeSWITCH Enterprise from SignalWire. Kamailio's home page calls it an open source SIP server under GPLv2+, able to handle thousands of call setups per second, and says it can be used to scale SIP-to-PSTN gateways, PBX systems, or media servers such as Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, or SEMS.

cites.label: A brief history of the Asterisk project

sections.h: rtpengine is the media proxy in this set
paragraphs: The rtpengine README calls it a proxy for RTP and other UDP media, meant to be used with the Kamailio SIP proxy, and a drop-in replacement for other RTP and media proxies. The only supported platform named there is GNU/Linux.

That split is the integration map: Kamailio for SIP signaling roles the project lists, including registrar, edge proxy, and WebSocket support for WebRTC, and rtpengine when the media needs a proxy that can rewrite SDP and bridge RTP with SRTP. Asterisk or FreeSWITCH is where a dialplan lives. Putting all four on one host is a choice these pages do not require.

lessons.title: Asterisk, PJSIP, and the dialplan
lessons.summary: chan_pjsip is the SIP channel driver. res_pjsip reads pjsip.conf. extensions.conf is the dialplan. The license page is GPL version 2, with a stated exception for AMI, AGI, and ARI.
objectives: Repeat the license page without turning it into legal advice

paragraphs: The res_pjsip page says the channel driver included with Asterisk 12 is chan_pjsip, and that it depends on res_pjsip and associated modules. res_pjsip is configured through pjsip.conf. The same page says extensions.conf is the dialplan and points at examples, outbound registration, and endpoint identification by IP address.

This lab does not paste a production endpoint. A study sketch that invents option names the page did not print would be a guess. When you configure a phone, open the configuration examples and the parameter reference on docs.asterisk.org for the version you run.

cites.label: A brief history of the Asterisk project

paragraphs: The license page says Asterisk is distributed under the GNU General Public License version 2 and is also available under alternative licenses negotiated directly with Digium, Inc. If you obtained Asterisk under the GPL, the page says the GPL applies to loadable Asterisk modules as well, except as that page defines.

The same page names the Asterisk Manager Interface (AMI), the Asterisk Gateway Interface (AGI), and the Asterisk REST Interface (ARI). It says Digium's belief is that applications using those protocols to manage or control an Asterisk instance do not have to be licensed under the GPL. That is the project's statement about its own license. It is not legal advice from this lab, and it is not a design for your module.

lessons.title: FreeSWITCH profiles, dialplan, and WebRTC
lessons.summary: The manual covers SIP profiles, the dialplan, codecs, media, WebRTC, and the Event Socket. There is an open source edition and an enterprise edition.
objectives: List what the opened manual says it teaches
Treat SignalWire's hosted service as a separate product from the open source build

illustration.title: What the manual introduction names
illustration.caption: Parameter tables in that manual are verified by its authors against the FreeSWITCH source. This lab does not copy those tables.

sections.h: What the manual says it covers
paragraphs: The FreeSWITCH users manual opened for this lab says it teaches a technically competent operator how to configure, set up, and run FreeSWITCH. The introduction lists SIP profiles, the dialplan, codec selection and negotiation, media handling, bundled applications, WebRTC, and the integration interfaces. It adds a module reference, troubleshooting, and programming with the Event Socket and embedded scripting.

The manual says every parameter, value, and default in it is verified against the FreeSWITCH source and the shipped default configuration. Use that manual for a parameter. Do not reconstruct a default from this lesson.

sections.h: Two editions, and a hosted product
paragraphs: The same introduction says FreeSWITCH ships in two editions and that the manual applies to both. Open Source FreeSWITCH is free and open source, with source and release builds on the FreeSWITCH releases page. FreeSWITCH Enterprise is the commercially supported edition from SignalWire.

The page also says SignalWire, founded by the FreeSWITCH team, operates this engine as a hosted platform with numbers, routing, conferencing, recording, and AI agents behind REST APIs and SWML. That hosted service is not the open source process on your server. An integration hook in the open source build that the manual names is the Event Socket.

lessons.title: Kamailio as the SIP server
lessons.summary: Kamailio is an open source SIP server under GPLv2+. Its page lists proxy, registrar, WebSocket, and scaling in front of a PBX.
objectives: Quote the role from the Kamailio home page
Name WebSocket support for WebRTC as a listed feature
Decide when the SIP server is Kamailio and the dialplan is elsewhere

illustration.title: Features named on the Kamailio home page
illustration.caption: This is the page's list, not a module index. Open the documentation page before you enable a module.
rows: Thousands of call setups per second

sections.h: The sentence on the home page
paragraphs: Kamailio, successor of OpenSER and SER, is described as an open source SIP server released under GPLv2+, able to handle thousands of call setups per second. The page says it can build large platforms for VoIP and realtime communications, including presence, WebRTC, and instant messaging.

It also says Kamailio can be used to scale SIP-to-PSTN gateways, PBX systems, or media servers like Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, or SEMS. Among the features it lists: TCP, UDP, and SCTP; TLS for voice, video, and text; WebSocket support for WebRTC; IPv4 and IPv6; SIMPLE instant messaging and presence; ENUM; least cost routing; load balancing; routing fail-over; accounting, authentication, and authorization.

sections.h: When this is the box you add
paragraphs: Use Kamailio when the problem is SIP signaling at the edge: registrar, proxy, load balancing, or a WebSocket listener in front of a PBX. The page claims that role. It does not claim to be the rtpengine media proxy, and it does not claim to be the Asterisk dialplan.

A browser from the WebRTC track can land on WebSocket support the Kamailio page lists. The SIP on that socket is still RFC 7118. Media for a WebRTC endpoint still follows DTLS-SRTP and ICE. If those packets need a media proxy, the rtpengine README is the next page, not another Kamailio slogan.

lessons.title: rtpengine and the integration map
lessons.summary: rtpengine proxies RTP, rewrites SDP, and can bridge ICE and SRTP. It runs on GNU/Linux and is meant to sit with Kamailio.
objectives: List media features the README states
Draw the SIP server beside the media proxy
Keep kernel forwarding as an optimization the README describes

illustration.title: Who touches the packet
illustration.caption: SIP stays on Kamailio. RTP can be forwarded by rtpengine, in kernel or in userspace.

layers.name: Control of the proxy
layers.detail: README: Kamailio rtpengine module, or the older rtpproxy-ng name.

layers.name: RTP
layers.detail: Userspace, or in-kernel forwarding with userspace fallback.

layers.name: Transform
layers.detail: ICE bridge, SDES, DTLS-SRTP, RTP to SRTP.

paragraphs: rtpengine is the Sipwise NGCP media proxy for RTP and other UDP media. It is meant to be used with Kamailio and can replace other RTP proxies. GNU/Linux is the only supported platform it names. Features in the README include IPv4 and IPv6, bridging between them, advertising a different address behind NAT, in-kernel packet forwarding with automatic fallback to userspace if the kernel module is unavailable, and HTTP, HTTPS, and WebSocket interfaces.

Used through the rtpengine module, or the older rtpproxy-ng name, the README adds full SDP parsing and rewriting, ICE support including a bridge between ICE-enabled and ICE-unaware agents, and SRTP support for SDES and DTLS-SRTP, including a bridge between RTP and SRTP user agents. Those are the reasons to add it. A deployment that does not need a media proxy does not need this process just because SIP is present.

Browser or phone to Kamailio for SIP. Kamailio to Asterisk or FreeSWITCH when a dialplan or PBX feature is required, which is the relationship Kamailio's own page describes. rtpengine beside Kamailio when SDP addresses must be rewritten or when ICE and SRTP need a bridge the README lists.

In-kernel forwarding is a performance path the README describes, with userspace fallback. This lab does not publish a packets-per-second figure for that path, because the README's sentence is low-latency and low-CPU, not a count. Confirm the current README before you enable a flag this page does not quote.

flow.title: SIP on Kamailio, RTP toward rtpengine

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Signaling hits the SIP server. The body still has the phone's media address.
steps.message:
INVITE sip:+15551212@203.0.113.20 SIP/2.0
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 203.0.113.10;branch=z9hG4bKrtp01
Max-Forwards: 70
From: "Alice" <sip:alice@example.com>;tag=rtp1
To: <sip:+15551212@example.com>
Call-ID: rtp-map@example.com
CSeq: 1 INVITE
Contact: <sip:alice@203.0.113.10>
Content-Type: application/sdp
Content-Length: 98

v=0
o=alice 1 1 IN IP4 203.0.113.10
s=-
c=IN IP4 203.0.113.10
t=0 0

steps.label: offer
steps.note: The Kamailio module asks rtpengine to rewrite SDP. This line is a study label, not a copy of the control protocol.
steps.message:
study control: offer
from 203.0.113.10:49170

steps.note: The proxy can advertise its own address. The README lists that NAT behavior.
steps.message: study control: media 203.0.113.20:30000

steps.note: The caller receives SDP that points at the proxy. RTP then goes to rtpengine, not through the SIP process.

lab.title: Read the rewritten c= line
lab.prompt: The offer points at the phone. The answer points at the proxy. That is the anchoring idea.
steps: Say which address the caller will send RTP toward.

fault.title: Kernel module missing, proxy declared down
fault.symptom: The kernel module failed to load. RTP still flows. An alarm says rtpengine is dead because kernel forwarding is off.
fault.log:
kernel module: unavailable
userspace forwarding: active
choices: The README says userspace is the fallback when the kernel module is unavailable
DTLS cannot run in userspace so delete SDP
fault.why: Fallback to userspace is a documented behavior, not proof the process exited.
fault.cause: The alarm treated one forwarding path as the whole proxy.
fault.fix: Confirm the process is up and userspace is forwarding. Restore the kernel module if you want that path. Read the current README for the flag names.
